title: Lesson 7 - Data Governance in Data 360: Data Spaces, RBAC vs ABAC, Tags, and Masking
description: Describe the principles of data ethics and governance, covering the governance mechanics (data spaces as boundaries, role-based versus attribute-based access control, tags and classification, and masking).

questions.question: An admin assigns a data space to a user's permission set, but the user still cannot see the records inside it. What is the most likely cause?
options: The data space was not published
Assigning a data space grants scope but not data access; an access policy must also grant it
Data spaces cannot be assigned to users
questions.explanation: A permission set data space assignment defines scope but does not by itself grant access to data; you create an access policy, often tag-based, to grant it. Modify All is unrelated to data space access.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes RBAC from ABAC in Data 360?
options: RBAC enforces row-level access, while ABAC manages feature access
RBAC governs access to features and platform capabilities, while ABAC enforces data access through policies
They are the same mechanism with different names
ABAC applies only to unstructured data
questions.explanation: RBAC controls who can use features and admin capabilities, while ABAC enforces object, field, and row-level data access plus masking through policies. Reversing them is the classic distractor.

questions.question: A policy must hide PII fields from all users except a compliance group. Which approach best fits?
options: Remove the fields from the data model
Tag the fields, classify them as PII, and bind a masking or access policy to the tag
Delete the fields in the source system
Rely on page layouts to hide the fields
questions.explanation: Data 360 attaches policies to tags, so tagging and classifying the fields and binding a policy grants context-aware access or masking. Removing fields from the model would break downstream use cases and is far too blunt.
